correctness.rationale: PASS. Reconstructed independence and maximality in the difference Cayley graph with forbidden residues ±1,±3,±4. Necessity: successive gaps cannot be 1,3,4 or >=10 (the vertex five inside an oversized gap is undominated), two adjacent 2 gaps produce forbidden distance four, and any 7/8/9 gap requires 2 on both sides to dominate its offset-two interior vertices. Sufficiency: all nonconsecutive selected vertices have shortest forward gap sum at least 7; endpoint distance steps ±1,±3,±4 and flanking 2 gaps cover all interior sites. Verified base sizes with direct graph enumeration and independently constructed cyclic gap words for n=5..17, including n=12 both size 2 and 3 and n=13 only size 3. Base pairs at n=14..18 and recurring insertion of a gap of 5 between two <=6 gaps give consecutive sizes at all n>=14. Double count ordered rooted gap words to obtain nW/k, with k=1 and 2 cyclic conventions checked. Finite tests are corroboration, not a proof of the infinite extension; the local dominance argument and induction supply that proof.
